questions.question: What are type annotations in Python, and how do you use the basic ones?
questions.title: Basic Type Annotations in Python
questions.direct_answer: Type annotations are optional hints that declare the expected type of a variable, parameter, or return value, e.g., name: str = 'Ada', or def greet(name: str) -> str. Python doesn't enforce them at runtime (they're hints, not checks) — a tool like mypy checks them statically. The basic built-in types are str, int, float, bool, bytes, and None. Annotations improve readability and enable IDE autocomplete and static type checking without changing Python's dynamic nature.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the annotation syntax (: and ->), the basic built-in types, and that Python doesn't enforce them at runtime (mypy does, statically).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking annotations are enforced at runtime, or using the old typing module (typing.List) instead of built-in list[int] (3.9+).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Annotations are : on variables/params and -> on returns; basic types str/int/float/bool/None. Optional, not runtime-enforced; mypy checks statically.

sections.title: Spoken Answer
sections.content: Type annotations are optional hints that declare the expected type of a variable, parameter, or return value. The syntax: name colon str equals Ada annotates a variable, and def greet of name colon str returns str declares a parameter and return type. Python does not enforce these at runtime — they're hints, not runtime checks — so a tool like mypy checks them statically before you run. The basic built-in types are str, int, float, bool, bytes, and None. Annotations improve readability, enable IDE autocomplete and refactoring, and let a type checker catch bugs early, all without changing Python's dynamic nature — you can still run code with wrong types; mypy will complain, Python won't. The common mistakes are thinking annotations are enforced at runtime, using the old typing module like typing.List instead of the built-in list of int which works from Python 3.9, and annotating but never running a checker, because annotations without mypy give no safety.

sections.title: Where Annotations Go
sections.content:
Annotations sit on variables (:) and function params/returns (: and ->); a checker reads them.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  V[name: str = 'Ada'] --> A[annotation]
  P[def f\(x: int\) -> str] --> A
  A -->|read by| M[mypy: static check]
  A -.not enforced at.-> R[runtime: ignores]
```

sections.title: Annotated variables and functions
sections.content:
```python
# (1) VARIABLE annotation: name: type = value.
name: str = "Ada"
count: int = 0
ratio: float = 0.5
active: bool = True

# (2) FUNCTION annotations: params with :, return with ->.
def greet(name: str, times: int = 1) -> str:
    return (f"Hi, {name}! " * times).strip()

# (3) Python does NOT enforce at runtime. This runs fine:
greet(123, "oops")          # no error at runtime
#   But `mypy file.py` will flag it: argument 1 has incompatible type.
```
